text:
Matthew Schaefer is a teenage defenseman doing things teenage defensemen don't do. He scored a hat trick in Tuesday's 5-1 win over Columbus, which Daily Faceoff noted makes him the third teenage NHL defender to record one, and he has six points in his last two games, per NHL.com's Stefen Rosner. Over his last ten games he has 15 points against 10.9 expected. Some of that is a heater. A lot of it is a franchise defenseman arriving.

The Islanders have won three straight with hat tricks in back-to-back games (Simon Holmstrom had one against Anaheim, his first, after a demotion to the fourth line). Mathew Barzal is back from a knee problem he called the hardest journey of his life, per the New York Post, on limited minutes for now.

Now the less fun part. New York is 10-6-4, but our expected points say about 19, not 24. The Islanders get 47% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and have allowed more than 14 fewer goals than their chances against suggest. That's goaltending: Ilya Sorokin and Semyon Varlamov have both been several goals above expected over their recent starts. The Bo Horvat line with Kyle Palmieri and Holmstrom drives play at 57%. Our playoff odds are 40%. As long as both goalies keep this up, the record holds; the chances say it's thin ice.
